Dated this the 12th day of April, 2024 Petitioners are accused Nos.1 and 4 in Crime No.1267 of 2023 of Kadinamkulam Police Station, registered for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.

The crime is registered on the basis of a complaint filed by the wife of the first petitioner that, after her marriage with the first petitioner on 07.08.2023, she had been constantly harassed by the accused.
The de facto complainant also alleged that the accused misappropriated gold ornaments weighing 27 sovereigns given by her parents at the time of marriage.
The specific allegation against the first petitioner is that, he tended to believe the words of his relatives/other accused and refused to protect the de facto complainant from them.
2. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submitted that all accused, other than the petitioners, were granted anticipatory bail by the jurisdictional Sessions Court.
It is submitted that the marriage was solemnised on 07.08.2023 and the complaint, leading to the registration of the crime, was lodged by the de facto complainant on 15.10.2023.
According to the Counsel, the ingredients necessary for attracting the offence under Section 498A of IPC is not made out from the FIR.
Finally it is submitted that if the petitioners are arrested and remanded, that would mete out undue hardship and injury to them.
3. I heard learned Public Prosecutor also.
4. Having gone through the FIR and having heard the learned Counsel for the petitioners, I find prima facie substance in the contentions urged.
It is doubtful whether the averments in the FIR are sufficient to attract the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
Of course, FIR is not a compendium of all facts and it is for the police to investigate and unearth the true facts.
In any event, in a case of this nature, custodial interrogation of the accused is not necessary.

Hence, the bail application is allowed with the following directions;
i) Petitioners shall appear before the investigating officer within two weeks.

(ii) The investigating officer shall interrogate the petitioners and in the event of their arrest, the petitioners shall be released on bail, on the petitioners executing bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty five thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
(iii) Petitioners shall not get involved in any similar offence during the pendency of the bail and shall not, in any manner, try to influence the witnesses or intimidate them.
(iv) Petitioners shall co-
operate with the investigation.
(v) The petitioners shall surrender their passport in the court below within one week.
If they do not hold a passport, they shall file an affidavit stating that fact.
If any one of the above condition is violated, the investigating officer will be at liberty to approach the jurisdictional court for cancellation of bail.
